label: Design
title: I also design *interfaces*.
lede: Six UI/UX case studies, designed solo in Figma in 2024 — concept work, not client projects. Supporting users all day makes you care a lot about screens that don't confuse people.

items.title: Joxich Hotel
items.tagline: Plan. Book. Travel. From “where to?” to “reserved” in four screens.
items.challenge: Booking a hotel online often means juggling cluttered listings, hidden fees and endless tabs. The goal was a booking flow that feels calm and trustworthy — search, compare and reserve without surprises.
items.approach: Started with low-fidelity wireframes to map the core journey — search, results, hotel details and sign-in — then built a reusable component library (navbar, date picker, location menu, hotel cards, FAQ accordion) before moving to high-fidelity screens.
items.outcome: A four-page, responsive-ready desktop flow with transparent pricing (nightly rate, taxes and total before you reserve), ratings and reviews at a glance, and similar-property suggestions.

decisions.title: Search first
decisions.detail: Location and date search sit on the hero, so the first action is the most important one.

decisions.title: Honest pricing
decisions.detail: Nightly price, discount, taxes and final total broken down before reservation.

decisions.title: Social proof
decisions.detail: Rating summary with distribution bars and recent reviews build trust fast.

items.title: CryptoMoney
items.tagline: One place to invest in crypto and manage your money — designed to make crypto feel approachable.
items.challenge: Crypto products tend to feel intimidating — dense charts, jargon, dark aggressive visuals. CryptoMoney needed to earn the trust of first-time investors while still feeling modern.
items.approach: A soft, muted lavender palette, friendly illustrations and short plain-language copy. Each benefit (invest, plan, manage) gets its own illustrated block, followed by three-step onboarding and app download calls to action.
items.outcome: A calm landing page with a signature card system — gradient debit cards that make the product tangible — plus a clear “how to get started” path and a news section.

decisions.title: Tangible product
decisions.detail: Gradient card designs show users what they actually get.

decisions.title: 3-step onboarding
decisions.detail: Create account → verify → start investing, explained up front.

decisions.title: Plain language
decisions.detail: Short, benefit-led copy instead of trading jargon.

items.title: JoxichClass
items.category: Edtech website — hobby classes for kids
items.tagline: Live hobby classes for kids, taught by creative mentors.
items.challenge: Parents want creative, trustworthy extracurricular learning for their kids — but hobby classes online are scattered and hard to compare. The site had to reassure parents while showing the fun of the classes.
items.approach: A clean navy-and-white system for credibility, paired with colourful hands-on class photography for energy. Classes and mentors are browsable in carousels with quick filters (All, Most Popular, Trending, Just Added).
items.outcome: A friendly landing page that moves parents from discovery to sign-up: email capture in the hero, class and mentor carousels, and a clear “why learn with us” section.

decisions.title: Email-first hero
decisions.detail: Sign-up is available from the very first screen.

decisions.title: Filterable carousels
decisions.detail: Classes and mentors browsable by popularity or recency.

decisions.title: Mentor credibility
decisions.detail: Real faces and specialisms build parent trust.

items.title: Discover Mountain
items.tagline: Explore the world — a travel site built around inspiration, activities and destinations.
items.challenge: Travel sites often lead with forms and prices. Discover Mountain needed to inspire first — make visitors want to go somewhere — and then make it easy to find the right trip.
items.approach: Full-bleed landscape photography and a deep teal palette for a calm, adventurous mood. A search bar on the hero, then an interactive activities list, a quote, testimonials and a masonry gallery of destinations.
items.outcome: An immersive single-page experience that balances inspiration and action, closing with a newsletter sign-up.

decisions.title: Search on the hero
decisions.detail: Destinations and things to do are one search away.

decisions.title: Activity explorer
decisions.detail: Walking, cycling, trekking, rafting and yoga — each with its own preview.

decisions.title: Destination gallery
decisions.detail: A masonry grid that sells the dream visually.

items.title: ProYoga Buddy
items.tagline: Ancient yoga practices, made easy to start.
items.challenge: Beginners often feel yoga isn't “for them”. ProYoga Buddy needed to feel calm and welcoming, explain its value quickly, and make choosing a membership simple.
items.approach: A serif/sans pairing (Lora + Raleway) and a soft periwinkle accent for a calm, editorial tone. Three pages — Home, Courses and About — built from a shared component set: buttons, email input and membership cards.
items.outcome: A serene three-page site with a clear path to joining: moody hero imagery, benefit tiles, straightforward pricing and a newsletter capture on every page.

decisions.title: Calm visual tone
decisions.detail: Serif headings and muted imagery set a mindful mood.

decisions.title: Simple pricing
decisions.detail: Two plans, three benefits each — easy to compare.

decisions.title: Consistent system
decisions.detail: Shared components across Home, Courses and About.

items.title: Personal Portfolio
items.tagline: A minimal, monochrome portfolio that lets the work do the talking.
items.challenge: A designer's portfolio has one job: get the work seen and make it easy to get in touch. Anything decorative competes with the projects.
items.approach: A monochrome palette and Work Sans keep the frame neutral. Four sections — About, Work, Blog and Contact — each fit in a single screen, with vertical section labels for quick orientation.
items.outcome: A focused one-page portfolio with project cards (tags and live links), a blog, a downloadable CV and a simple contact form.

decisions.title: Neutral frame
decisions.detail: Greys only, so project visuals stand out.

decisions.title: One screen per section
decisions.detail: About, Work, Blog, Contact — no scroll fatigue.

decisions.title: Clear actions
decisions.detail: Download CV, view live projects, send a message.
